recognition.difference: The book states this as an oscillation result for $\zeta$ alone: Theorem 15.2 says $\psi(x) - x = \Omega_\pm(x^{\Theta - \varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$, where $\Theta$ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of $\zeta$, and the library's form is the contrapositive of its $\Omega_+$ half. The book assumes the bound for all large $x$ and takes the error term $\psi(x) - x$ of one function; the library assumes it only on windows $[Y, Y^{1+\delta}]$ for arbitrarily large $Y$, for a weighted sum over a family of characters of the smoothed sums $\sum \Lambda(n)\chi(n)(y/n - 1)$ with main terms removed. The textbook proof also expands at a fixed point, but it sums the whole Taylor series and rearranges it, which uses the sign for all large $x$; the library's proof uses one coefficient of high order at a time, whose weight lies in a single window up to a small tail. The book's proof of Lemma 15.1 is one sentence: the proof of Theorem 1.7 "can be adapted".
